name: Russell Ebert
bio: Widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers produced in South Australia, Russell Ebert was renowned for his courage, elite disposal, durability, and leadership. He holds the record for most games played for Port Adelaide and is the only four-time Magarey Medallist.
trivia: Ebert played one season in the VFL with North Melbourne in 1979 before returning to Alberton to captain-coach Port Adelaide.

name: Malcolm Blight
bio: A mercurial genius capable of unbelievable feats, Malcolm Blight won the Magarey Medal with Woodville before starring for North Melbourne in the VFL. Famous for kicking a post-siren goal from 75m out in 1976.
trivia: Blight won the 1978 Brownlow Medal while playing at North Melbourne, uniting both major individual league awards.

name: Barrie Robran
bio: Possessing sublime skill, balance, and football intelligence, Barrie Robran is revered as footballing royalty in South Australia. Despite injuries curtailing his career, his dominance on the field remains legendary.
trivia: Robran was named Legend status in the Australian Football Hall of Fame in 2001.

name: Ken Farmer
bio: Ken Farmer is one of the most prolific goalscorers in Australian rules football history. He kicked 100+ goals in eight consecutive seasons and remains the leading goalkicker in SANFL history with 1,417 majors.
trivia: Farmer kicked 10 or more goals in a match 23 times during his legendary career.

name: Fos Williams
bio: A towering figure in SA football, John James 'Fos' Williams transformed Port Adelaide into a football powerhouse. As player-coach, he instilled a fierce winning ethos known as the 'Port Adelaide Creed'.
trivia: Fos coached Port Adelaide to six successive premierships from 1954 to 1959.

name: Rick Davies
bio: A giant of the SANFL. A dominant ruckman with supreme tactical awareness and penetrating left-foot kicking, he once kicked 151 goals in a single season for South Adelaide in 1983.
trivia: Davies crossed to Hawthorn late in his career and won a VFL premiership in 1983.

name: Stephen Kernahan
bio: Before leading Carlton to VFL/AFL premierships as captain, Stephen 'Sticks' Kernahan was a powerhouse forward for Glenelg, terrorising SANFL defences with his aerial strength.
trivia: Kernahan was named captain of the AFL Team of the Century.

name: Mark Mickan
bio: An inspirational ruckman renowned for his fierce competitiveness and leadership. Mark Mickan won the Magarey Medal in 1985 for West Adelaide and later captained the inaugural Brisbane Bears side.
trivia: Mickan returned to South Australia to captain-coach North Adelaide to the 1991 SANFL premiership.

name: Bruce Lindner
bio: A high-flying and exceptionally accurate forward who played a vital role in West Adelaide's famous 1983 SANFL premiership. Later crossed to Geelong in the VFL before becoming an inaugural player for the Adelaide Crows in 1991.
trivia: Lindner kicked 4 goals in Adelaide's historic inaugural VFL/AFL match against Hawthorn in 1991.

name: Bruce Abernethy
bio: Renowned for his silky skills, blonde flowing locks, and versatility across the wing and half-back line, Bruce Abernethy was a cornerstone of Port Adelaide's success before enjoying stints in Melbourne and finishing with the Adelaide Crows.
trivia: Abernethy won four SANFL premierships with Port Adelaide and played in the Crows' inaugural squad.

name: Bruce Winter
bio: A fierce competitor and tenacious rover who was the heartbeat of Sturt midfields during the golden era under Jack Oatey, later finishing his illustrious career across town at Norwood.
trivia: Winter was renowned for his courage in packs and tireless defensive pressure.

name: Rudi Mandemaker
bio: A towering ruckman who carried the ruck load for Central District during their rise as a powerhouse in the SANFL, earning a VFL stint with Footscray in the mid-1980s before returning to Elizabeth.
trivia: Mandemaker was one of the premier tap ruckmen of his era in South Australian football.

name: Michael Coligan
bio: A rugged and dependable utility player for South Adelaide who gave his all week in and week out at Noarlunga Oval, earning a VFL opportunity with Footscray.
trivia: Coligan was admired for his adaptability across both backline and forward line roles.

name: Kym Hodgeman
bio: An electrifying, skilful rover for Glenelg who tormented opposition defences with his pace and goal sense, before crossing to Victoria to play for North Melbourne.
trivia: Hodgeman was a key figure in Glenelg's high-scoring, entertaining teams of the late 1970s and 1980s.

name: Neville Roberts
bio: A rock-solid defender known as 'The Ghost' due to his ability to seemingly appear out of nowhere to intercept opposition forward thrusts. Starred for West Torrens and later won a premiership with Norwood.
trivia: Roberts represented South Australia with distinction in State of Origin football.

name: Danny Jenkins
bio: A fiercely competitive defender who was an integral part of Norwood's legendary 'pecking order' teams under Neil Kerley and Garry McIntosh, renowned for his uncompromising spoils and toughness.
trivia: Jenkins played in Norwood's famous 1978 and 1982 SANFL premiership sides.
